svg.text: Build 1 on a breadboard: the chip, the screen and the knob. No jacks yet.
19 jumper wires. Plug them in number order with the USB cable unplugged. Red = 3.3 V, black = ground; the other colors are only to tell wires apart.
Looking down at the Pico's top (the side with the chips), USB to the left. Pin 1 is the bottom-left pin, next to the USB plug; pin 40 is right above it.
go by the labels printed on it; the order varies.
Some print SDA for DIN and SCL for CLK.
wire 1: pin 36 (3V3) round the end of the board to the red + rail at the bottom
a dot = the end goes in that hole
Green: the 5 holes in one column are joined inside, like one wire. A wire in any of
them touches the Pico pin in that column. The Pico sits across the middle gap, so each
pin gets its own column with 2 free holes on the outside edge (rows a-b and i-j).
The middle gap splits each column in two: the top half and the bottom half never touch.
Red: a rail runs the whole length. Wire 1 puts 3.3 V on the red + rail and wire 2 puts
ground on the blue - rail; then every red wire and every black wire can go in anywhere
along them. On some long boards the rail is cut in the middle (a break in the red line):
plug everything into the same half, or bridge the break with a short wire.
Never: a wire from VBUS (pin 40) or VSYS (pin 39). Those are 5 V and the screen and the chip want 3.3 V.
